_comment: Hot-path criterion baseline: the median ns of each bench in crates/bench/benches/hot_path.rs, keyed by the id the bench gives `bench_function` (criterion's `full_id`), gated by `make bench-check` (check_regression.py) at `tolerance_pct`.

Host: the Apple M4 Pro. Re-baselined 2026-09-25 at 5f2140f, each value the median of three `make bench-check` runs (warm-up 1 s, 2 s, 50 samples) with the launchd engine running, as it always is. The values before were a 2026-05-19 Linux aarch64 sandbox run that the check never compared on this Mac: it looked for results under a path this criterion does not write.

book/apply_n8_middle and strategy/latency_arb_on_tick_no_fire have not been the sandbox's 0.94 / 1.66 ns since phase 8a: the initial commit's code (02db7a6) measures 1.07 / 1.69 ns on the M4, 5f2140f 1.99 / 2.47 ns. Both benches repeat one tick, so every apply after the first is stale, and D10 (503606f) made a stale apply count itself (`stale_drops += 1`, a read-modify-write per call) where it used to return.
Not gated: ring/spsc_rtt_tick and ring/spsc_stream_tick, two threads that macOS places as it likes (103-122 ns and 9-11 ns across sessions); docs/risk-policy.md records them.
Re-baseline when a change moves a number on purpose: three `make bench-check` runs, each value their median, and the reason recorded here and in docs/risk-policy.md.
